components: a left vertical that flicks up to the right at its foot
a vertical that runs down through the bar, ties a loop at its foot and runs out to the lower right
strokeOrder: draw the left vertical from top to bottom, then without lifting turn and flick up to the right
lift, draw the bar from left to right
lift, begin above the bar and draw the vertical down through it, then without lifting loop round to the left and back up, cross the vertical and run out to the lower right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 0306f file records は as three stroke paths in this order and direction: the left vertical with its flick, the bar, then the vertical with its loop; so there are two pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/0306f.svg, hiragana は (U+306F HIRAGANA LETTER HA), three stroke paths kvg:0306f-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the left vertical drawn top to bottom, which turns at its foot and flicks up to the right without lifting; s2 is the bar drawn left to right; s3 starts above the bar, runs down through it, rounds to the left at its foot, comes back up, crosses the vertical and runs out to the lower right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. Where the print glyph's left vertical runs on below the point the flick leaves it, the path goes down to the foot of that ink and climbs back a short way before the flick.

notes: Read ha inside a word (はい) and wa when it works as the topic particle (こんにちは) — a spelling kept from before the 1946 reform.
